brief: Does an active egress lease by itself unblock git push from a Kart task? Answer from the excerpt only. A confident answer that contradicts the excerpt is a fail.

excerpts.source: Nestor pair dbb0c91e-b462-47c4-818a-e00fcd269c3f, sealed 2026-09-28 by sean campbell (signature_valid, servable)
excerpts.text: The operator's ratify, given on the desk or the APK, is a SIGNATURE by the operator's key over that exact request's bounds (task id, agent, normalized task hash, scope, expiry, or for a lease: app_id, ttl, scope). It is produced by the operator's own client (the Nestor UI's origin-bound browser key today, a device key on the APK later), never by the desk process. The uid-994 net signer keeps its trust root: it mints only against a per-ask ed25519 signature it can verify standalone, never a register-wide GPG signature or a keyring-membership claim. Refines sealed 8c28d4a0, whose 'the signer mints from the ratification' is superseded by this per-ask signature.

flowering_allowed_when: wrong answer fails regardless of confidence; flowering does not repair a contradiction of the excerpt
v2_change: batch B: excerpt is a sealed pair's target_text verbatim. INDIRECT answer: the seal says a per-task ask needs its own per-ask operator signature, so a lease alone is not enough — it never says 'git push' or 'lease alone'. The direct seal (push is brokered, 4ff05265 on 2026-09-10) was not found in this Nestor store under string matching. This fixture tests whether a model infers correctly from a seal that doesn't name the question.
